facts.value: The origins of bioinformatics date back to the mid-20th century and were related to the development of molecular biology and the discovery of the structure of DNA by James Watson and Crick in 1953.
In the 1950s, organic chemistry, biology, and computing started to develop structural algorithms for clarity and prediction of protein structure.
In the 1960s and 1970s, the way biological data was stored saw a tremendous change.
Well-known examples are the Protein Data Bank (PDB) and the GenBank DNA sequence database.
